issues.detail: The Greek 'κακως εχοντας' (having taken up/carried badly/roughly) refers to the *manner* in which they were carrying the people. The Vietnamese translation 'đau nằm trên cái giường' (painfully lying on the bed) introduces a specific detail ('bed') and an interpretation of 'badly' as 'painful' that is not present in the Greek text.

The Greek 'περιδραμοντες' (running about/rushing) implies a sense of urgency or running. The Vietnamese 'chạy khắp' captures 'running', but the phrase 'bắt đầu khiêng' (started carrying) slightly softens the continuous/active nature of the rushing movement described in the Greek.
